reviews.text: At £17 its a little steep of a price for the amount of Game here. You run through 7 ish battles 3 times on a campaign whilst developing your own army. The relics and consumables add some variety but it feels like the balance of challenge is all over the place. A campaign is either a stomp or ended by a sudden difficulty spike depending on RNG. Battles are fun but can feel tedious when its an obvious victory and you still take big losses. AI in battles is a little dumb. Its easy to exploit their targeting and pathfinding. Settlement raids are easily exploited as you can funnel the enemy out of a single chokepoint. BUT! For a game with lots of planned feature updates (New Factions / Multiplayer) ;there is a lot of fun to be had hear even at release. If you enjoy total war / slay the spire and want a casual version of both this is a great choice!

Let me start of by saying i like the game. I played the demo when it first came out and while i saw some bugs I honestly couldnt wait to play more of this. But as soon as i now play the main game, get into the battle and use the ALT-DRAG function to move my units forward they turn to the side going into pencil formation. THAT WAS THE SAME BUG I ENCOUNTERED DURING THE FIRST DEMO! How is this still a problem? Moving your army around is like 90% of the gameplay. If not even the most basic of bugs have been fixed then I cannot in good conscious recommend this game to anyone. Edit: It also is still impossible to move units trough other units. So if you want to move a unit up from behind your archers say then a few men may walk around the edges but the main body of the unit will be stuck behind the archers. They will also not even try to go around them.

还不错的游戏，借鉴了战锤全面战争，操作手感较为类似。 有几个建议 1.增加点全面战争的操作习惯，比如空格显示部队前往的站位明确位置。 2.调整一下平衡，虽然休息火堆处随机一个单位升级真的很强但是感觉有点太强大了。。。然后同一种族更高级稀有度单位差异其实特别小，只是微微调整了属性，可以加入更多特质以及或者通过事件给予一些特殊BUFF给老单位持续整场战役的那种，不然新单位一上来然后一升级我老单位完全没没有留的必要了。 3.攻城战我感觉就和送福利一样，拿远程大炮开一个门敌人疯狂往外送，虽然也不是不行但是按道理守城不应该占点防守的吗，直接出来排队枪毙我感觉完全没难度。。。（顺便说下敌人巨龙，巨人我大炮两轮直接灭了是否有点太简单了。。。） 4.虽然这个游戏是迷你全面战争，但是感觉是数据太高接战基本很快解决，也可能是我才玩了第一个难度？但是我几炮秒了对面也太快了吧，近战可以肉一点伤害都调低一点我感觉更有战斗的感觉，不然一打起来敌人瞬间全跑了，特别是敌人的农民部队跑过来的路上我射两下直接跑路了，跑了也不会跑回来这个做简化我理解但是也打的太快太快了吧。 整体来说手感还行，目前没有英雄只有首领BUFF的概念，官方后续会加入法术，就是感觉打的有点快没沉浸感。 价格凑合，我买的和另一款有的捆绑包三十多还行吧。 官方认真更新让内容更加丰富我觉得未来可期，比较老了玩全面战争太久有点累，这个肉鸽元素快节凑还不错凑合玩玩碎片时间。 对了，如果能出多人合作肉鸽我觉得非常有意思！！！弥补一下全面战争和朋友打好几十回合都不一定能在一个战场相遇的遗憾、望采纳！ Pretty good game overall! I can clearly see the Total War: Warhammer inspiration, and the controls feel quite similar. I do have a few suggestions: 1. Quality of Life controls from Total War: Please add some standard Total War control habits, like pressing the Spacebar to clearly display the destination and facing direction of selected units. It makes managing formations so much easier. 2. Balance and Unit Progression: While getting a random unit upgrade at the rest bonfire is really cool, it feels a bit overpowered right now. Also, the difference between lower and higher rarity units of the same race is negligible—just slight stat bumps. I’d suggest adding more distinct traits to higher-tier units, or allowing campaign-wide permanent buffs/traits through events for veteran units. As it stands, there’s zero reason to keep an old unit when a newly recruited one gets an immediate upgrade and out-stats them. A “veterancy” system would give players a reason to preserve their starting units. 3. Siege Battles and Monster Balance: Siege battles currently feel like free giveaways. I just use artillery to breach the gate, and the defenders suicide-rush out in a line to get slaughtered. I get the logic, but shouldn’t the defenders have an advantage by holding defensive positions? Queueing up to get shot to pieces makes sieges completely devoid of challenge… (On a side note, is it just me, or are enemy Dragons and Giants way too fragile? Two salvos from my artillery outright deleted them. That feels way too easy.) 4. Battle Pacing and Damage Output: Even though this is a “Mini Total War,” the damage values feel way too high, making engagements resolve far too quickly. Maybe it’s because I’m only on the first difficulty, but obliterating the enemy in a few salvos feels abrupt. I think melee units need more health/sustain, and overall damage should be toned down to give battles more of a “meat grinder” feel. Right now, once fighting starts, the enemy breaks and routes almost instantly. Low-tier units like peasants will charge in, take two arrows, and instantly route—and they never come back. I understand simplifying the morale mechanics, but the fights just end *way* too fast to feel immersive. Overall, the game feel is decent. Right now, there are no heroes, just faction leader buffs, though I saw the devs plan to add magic later. My main issue is just the breakneck battle pace killing the immersion. The price is fair—I bought it in a bundle with another game for around 30 RMB, which is reasonable. If the game keep updating and fleshing out the content, this game has a lot of potential. As an older gamer, playing actual Total War for hours gets exhausting, so this Roguelike spin with a faster pace is a nice fit for my fragmented free time. One last idea: If you guys could add a Multiplayer Co-op Roguelike mode, that would be incredible! It would perfectly make up for the frustration of playing Total War with a friend and taking dozens of turns just to finally end up in the same battle. Please consider this!

I made this review because I am a player of Total War first and foremost, and I am ONLY looking for very close alternatives. Thus, regardless of whoever made it, the final products will always be measured against the 25-years old franchise. If you enjoys this game, go ahead, but this is a [b] review for a very specific group of players.[/b] The goods: very good TW-like troop controls. semi-decent loading and performance in relative to the simplistic artstyle, and the UI is great. The bads: army running sounds is very off. The actual units and controls are far too simplistic, and you can essentially cheese the AI by camping on the corner, just like in Total War, and there is very little customization of your troops or your faction as a whole. You can blob troops up and shoot into your own blobs without repercussion. The 'siege' maps are just boring. The big issue is faction variety - if you use Custom Battle mode, test them out, for each race have an overall same-y roster except for a few artillery pieces. The fact this game doesn't count as EA means it considers itself complete, so even if the dev promise magic and some future content, I just don't see myself liking the 'finished' product with this gameplay. Now, onto the core of my negative review. This game, like Master of Command and Strategos, the majority of TW-lite games either lacking in campaign or battle. This game is very simplistic in both animations and unit variety. I played it for less than 2 hours and KNOW I will never play it again, because the inherent gameplay loops isn't for me. The actual troops control and stats are hindrances or long-term enjoyment compared to roguelike card battlers that can manipulative and weave complexity and conditionings into their individual playthroughs. Sure, you can say it's mostly indie and they do not have a big studio budget, but there's a reason why big budget games are good. It's impressive for a solo dev project, but it is essentially stealing from every other game in lore, design, gameplay, and genres, games that have done it better in their own market. I prefer to have a 100-hours long campaign rather than roguelike smaller campaigns, or a linear campaign with a few variants. For the price, get it on sale. Or just get an older TW game. UPDATE: I refunded it.

The main reason I can't recommend it, is because the meta-progression feels really, *really* bad. First of all, you have to deposit currency from your run to use it for meta-progression. This means that you have to intentionally hamper your current run to benefit your meta-progression. It's not just about picking up something like an XP boost instead of a power boost, but literally burning your run-currency to use it between games instead. This feels really bad. In addition, a lot of the bonuses are really boring, and really tiny. For example, buying a meta progression for an extra reserve slot is 250 gold. Another meta-progression costs 50 gold and gives you 1 extra gold per run. This means it'll need 50 runs to pay itself back, or 250 runs to pay for the reserve slot. Of course, a gold early (starting gold) is better than a gold later, but it still just *feels bad*. It works in an idle game, but this isn't an idle game. Honestly I think they just should scrap this entire idea and have meta-currency obtained separately from gold (for example have a % of your spent gold during a run become meta-currency when you finish a run).

游戏组合模式还是挺有意思的，但是缺点还是很突出 1.平衡性问题比较严重，破甲远程过于强了，基本齐射秒一切，弄得前排必须是持盾，要不动不动就被齐射带走了，就破甲远程火力有多猛，3队远程齐射我，我边路的骑兵还在绕圈冲锋，前排已经被射死1队半了 2.抽卡的等级跟不上游戏难度，比如怪已经多半都是紫色怪了，给的还只是绿色卡，最后只能选择收编野怪，弄得种族没意义了，基本就是这关是什么野怪你就用什么兵的节奏，包括商店售卖的卡片也是，价格过于昂贵，没法用本族的兵组出套路 3.局外升级和局内购买都是用金币，本意可能是想让大家在尽量少消耗金币的情况下通关，但是实际变成需要再低级难度用简单的种族刷金币，然后买满局外升级后挑战高难度，另外局外升级内容过于简单了，各项升级的效果也参差不齐，除了几个开槽位的，其他那些减金币消耗的效果与实际消耗相比真是杯水车薪 4.自动战斗因为损耗过大，没有实际意义，而目前战斗地形非常简单，包括空间、视野、地形起伏等都没有，导致战术基本就是前排推进，后排集火，骑兵绕边路偷后排，打久了非常无聊 5.兵种数值设计有问题，比如近战攻防，除了少量杂鱼兵攻防在20/20左右，少量高级兵在40/40，其他大部分兵种攻防都是30/30这档，然后能给兵升级威望就相当于给这个小兵升等级，每升一级攻防直接加10/10，然后1点攻防差影响4%命中，所以哪怕是灰色小兵升到3级攻防+20后，能把敌人命中直接减到10%，简直跟神一样，而高级兵只是会多一点破甲、反步兵之类的技能，但是没有攻防完全打不到，所以近战兵对打攻防就是天，你攻防高对面20，对面兵打你命中只有10%，你打对面命中90%，完全碾压。然后远程就更变态了，远程只看自己命中，和对方是否持盾，而破甲能无视对方护甲减伤，所以导致破甲远程伤害爆表，只要把命中堆上去点，或者多来几队兵，那伤害就是实打实全乎对方脸上。然后是射程，一般远程兵射程在50-100，而炮兵射程一般是125，这就导致远程走两步就能射到炮兵，而炮兵非常脆，1个远程兵射2下就能直接秒掉炮兵，导致炮兵没有什么存在意义，尤其是远程兵还有装备可以加射程，加完比炮兵射程还远 6.通关过程中的节点虽然有好几种，但是大部分没有什么实际意义，增加战力主要还是靠战斗后的免费抽卡和收编，以及篝火里的威望升级，游戏、事件、商店，城寨几乎提供不了太多帮助 7.兵种技能里游骑兵这个技能着实没有什么用，效果就是战斗前排兵布阵的时候有游骑兵技能的兵可以放到限制范围以外，但是你把少量游骑兵兵种扔到对面附近，基本就是送死，而电脑还非常喜欢这么干，打精灵、武士的野怪，上来基本就是先调头清理后面的几个游骑兵，然后在回头对付敌人大部队，我觉得设计师要是想做奇兵，就需要设计视野和隐蔽效果，要不没有任何实际意义 总之，目前存在的问题比较多，初玩还有点新鲜感，但是打个2局就只剩各种吐槽了

The roguelike portion suffers from a severe lack of content — you’ll see everything the game has to offer within 2–3 runs, and the so‑called “random events” are basically nonexistent, leaving almost no variation between playthroughs. The game also throws an unnecessarily large number of characters at you, yet none of them feel distinct. Melee units without shields, even at the highest rarity, get instantly deleted by ranged attacks and have no real purpose. The RTS portion — supposedly the core of the game — is plagued by bugs and baffling design issues. Unit formations jitter and refuse to stay where you place them, group movement scrambles formations for no reason, squads drift far off the intended path if even one member gets stuck, and under certain conditions units simply stop fighting altogether. And these are just the issues I ran into quickly; I’m sure there are many more. Overall, the game isn’t worth your time.

Avid RTS player. The game is fun overall, maxed it out in about 30 hours, probably could have done it in 24 or so. Gameplay loop does get quite repetitive, but I feel this would be a good intro into RTS for people who may not enjoy it as much as those that are very hardcore. The 3 act 12 chapter length is much too short with little variation. I didn't lose a single campaign run which makes me feel it's not all that rogue-like. Some of the balancing is just way too broken for certain units, and the AI gets very predictable where you can win the battles the same way pretty much every time. Some items are way too strong, like pumpkin pie is an instant win on the Godking difficulty, so being able to start with something like that is a bit crazy. The meta progression, doesn't really help all that much, but it's nice little things that help you build up to better take on the higher difficulty levels. Really you just play on low difficulties a couple times to build up a bank, get the upgrades, then steamroll through god-king. It's a nice cozy game RTS in my opinion, but having to play through the same campaign almost 20 times to get all the achievements can be quite a slog. Overall it is worth the price tag, and for a one-man show (minus the marketing people) it is pretty impressive, but don't expect anything ground breaking. Really it needs some major love and balancing to make it what it can be. Really doesn't seem like its in a full release state, but it is very enjoyable and has good vibes. Solid 6.5/10

This is one of those games where I wish there was a neutral rating option. I will opt for a thumbs up because the developer is making a very earnest effort to create a fun blend of a Total War like strategy game and a roguelite campaign. That said, be prepared to get go back in time to early Total War titles in terms of balance and mechanics quality. Currently, both factions and units are wildly unbalanced. Dwarves are absolutely devastating because the game favors raw stat blocks and heavy infantry. Monsters are terrible as they can be easily shot down by any (including tier 1) archers and they completely fail at doing what they should be best at, eating heavy infantry. Sieges are basic at best and just one siege engine makes them essentially a free win (enemies literally will charge you once you break their first gate, through that single broken gate, kindly choking their line and trickling out to you). Cavalry charges don't work quite right. Ranged units will sometimes continue shooting even when engaged in melee. Pretty much every major issue TW games have suffered from over the years, this game suffers from now (proving how difficult the mechanics of this genre are to get right). I really hope to see this game develop and fix many of the balance and mechanics issues. Right now playing it makes me wish someone would just develop the roguelite campaign system for TW3 (or a similar title) that already has proper balancing and the mechanical kinks worked out.

[h1]爬塔的外皮，全战的内核，新奇的体验[/h1] 虽然现在爬塔游戏多如牛毛，但是绝大多数在战斗形式上还是以卡牌、战棋或者是类幸存者玩法为主。而本作正如其游戏名《桌上谈兵》所表述的那样，玩家犹如在一张大的棋盘上探索，而当抵达例如“遭遇战”之类的点位时，若选择手动战斗就会切入到可供玩家完全微操的大战场中，也有着各种兵种克制机制与战斗模式，整体玩法算得上的“全面战争”青春版。本作也有很强的肉鸽属性，基本上也是越战越强的存在。游戏为正式版发行，官方还承诺永无付费DLC，一次购买即可获得完整内容。 在画面风格上，本作采用的是3D低多边形风格，整体观感像是置身在卡通风的中世纪之中。玩家初始可以从各大军团派系中选择英雄并组建队伍出征。不同的军团有着专属的战役和战斗BUFF，英雄则有专属单位和自身的效果加成，主要是要配合相应的兵种以产生最大化的效果。 正如前面我提到的，在流程上玩家会以一个俯视角的爬塔路线不断往前推进。点位上有类型游戏常见的战斗、事件、商店、城镇、篝火以及宝藏等等，这方面看上去倒还是挺传统的。不过很多的事件抉择采用了投骰检定的方式，有一定的随机性。但是制作组又加入了消耗金币进行结果修正的方式弥补，有钱就可以为所欲为吗？ 与其他游戏相比，本作最显著的特点无疑是其战斗方式。具体来说，当玩家正儿八经的选择手动战斗的时候，会切入到一个有着自由镜头和可切换视角的大战场之中，排兵布阵展开两军对垒。玩家可以自由调整各兵种的方位，当然亘古不变的真理是冲锋骑兵和T在前，射手、炮兵队在后。除了有着完整的一套伤害修正、克制机制外，各个兵种也有着独特的指令或特性。像是弓箭手有着齐射、自动开火等4种攻击模式，而像是炮兵的炮击伤害竟然还是有友伤的，大面积炮兵攻击时尤其需要注意我方部队的位置。此外还有士气值的概念，士气归零时部队就会溃散而逃。而有效削减敌方士气的常规手段进行背后偷袭和夹击。不过敌方AI也绝不会如此轻易让你瓮中捉鳖，还是需要把握一定的时机和微操。 但是这种战斗模式也就产生出了一个问题，那就是战斗相对来讲显得比较烦琐，一局爬塔下来全是手动无疑是比较累的。也因此制作组还配合推出了自动战斗模式，且是那种完全不需要进入战场的自动，还会在面板上就告诉你自动战斗的结果。不过从本质上来说，选择自动就需要面对一些不可控的战损。但在绝对的部队、装备等属性碾压下，其实自动战斗确实能省去很多的时间和操作。 整体来说，本作就像是桌游+肉鸽爬塔+全战的超强结合体，玩法上还是非常新奇有趣的。不过目前各个派系军团以及兵种的差异度还有待提升，并应该适当提升下局外成长的强度。 [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42276832//]鸿源鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 会当逢佳游，始可见鸿源。 [/b][/u]

At the current state of early access I can't really recommend it. It's severely lacking in content/Variety, sieges are a joke, most factions feel very similar and you mostly play each fight the same way with little difference. This game needs to: 1. Improve Sieges, Something like Medieval 2's cities randomly generated with the specific Faction the town belongs to would be cool as hell and actually give it an edge over Creative Assembly. 2. Make the game harder, at the moment there are simply far too many options and ways to heal your troops in my opinion and even losing a unit rarely matters because you can replace them after every battle. 3. The whole retreat/Morale system needs a desperate rework. It just doesn't feel satisfying that the moment a unit retreats, it no longer matters for the battle so their units just pass through unopposed without anyone trying to attack them. It also doesn't matter how many enemies you kill, you just need to break their morale which feels especially stupid when you break the morale of undead. Not to mention you can just slap an outrider unit right into their artillery/archers at game start, kill the target and without repercussion of any kind click the retreat button which immediately renders that unit invincible for the rest of the fight as it now leaves the map safely despite being completely surrounded. Now I get this game is still early access and a solo dev is behind it, so development can be tricky/time intensive, but before I can recommend this game to anyone these 3 Issues kinda have to be resolved in some form. I want this game to succeed so I'll check it out again in a year or two and update my review by then.

I genuinely went into this expecting to refund it. Not because it looked bad, but because I don't normally gel with roguelikes. And with this being essentially Total War without the grand campaign, I didn't expect to enjoy it. BUT I absolutely love the total war battles formula, so I bought it. The concept sounded brilliant, but the first couple of battles just didn't click with me, which I fully expected. I wasn't really enjoying it and thought it might not be for me. Thankfully, I stuck with it because after a few runs on Easy, everything started to make sense and I ended up having a blast. I still need more time with it to see how the other factions (beyond the Elves) play and how the meta progression develops, but my first impressions have completely changed. The easiest way to describe Tabletop Tavern is Total War: Warhammer meets Slay the Spire. You build an army in this fantasy setting with Elves, Dwarves, Orcs, Humans and so on, throughout a roguelike campaign, recruiting new units, finding powerful upgrades and relics, then putting your force to the test in real-time battles where positioning, counters, and synergies actually matter. The tabletop presentation is fantastic, and it's incredibly satisfying watching an army you've carefully put together steamroll the enemy... or get completely wiped because of one bad decision. There's plenty of replayability thanks to the different factions, heroes, random events, and the sheer number of builds you can create. Every run feels different enough that I always wanted to jump straight into another. If you're a fan of Total War, roguelikes like Slay the Spire, or strategy games in general, I'd absolutely recommend giving this a go. Just don't make the same mistake I almost did. Give it a few battles before deciding whether it's for you.

[h1]把《全面战争》塞进肉鸽爬塔里[/h1] 肉鸽爬塔游戏玩过不少，卡牌的、战棋的、幸存者的都试过了，但像《桌上谈兵》这样把即时战略也揉进肉鸽爬塔的，记忆里倒真是独此一家了。 《桌上谈兵》的模式说着倒也简单，开局选择不同种族的英雄，不同的英雄都会带着自己种族的军队，然后就可以开始沿着爬塔的路线向上推进，各种战斗、事件、宝藏、城镇、商店等节点遍布整个树叉路线上，我们根据自己军队的实力选择路线即可。 有意思的是，在《桌上谈兵》这里遭遇战斗，是会进入像《全面战争》那样的即时战略战场的，我们需要我们麾下的军队类型进行排兵布阵，战斗的时候还得一个部队一个部队的安排他们的行动，骑兵冲锋、长枪防骑、弓箭手齐射、炮兵轰炸，各种兵种都有自己的战斗定位。 而且各部队不仅有血量，还有士气系统，一旦士气崩溃便会溃逃，而背后包抄、夹击敌军则能快速瓦解对方阵线，而且还有攻城战和兵种相克等的机制。别看游戏建模略微粗糙，战斗起来还真有《全面战争》那样的味道！ 当然，即时战略苦手的小伙伴也不用怕，游戏还提供了自动战斗的方式，懒得动手的时候让电脑自己进行数据碰撞，也是个不错的选择，只是数据碰撞时不时还是会出现较为离谱的战损就是了，很容易影响我们后面的爬塔计划。 游戏给各个种族都配置了不少等阶的兵种，按颜色的话就是白（普通）绿（罕见）紫（稀有）金（传说）四个等阶，不同等阶实力天差地别！而且相同品质的相同兵种还能合成升级，又提升了一点部队养成的乐趣。 我们能够通过战斗、事件或者俘虏系统不断扩充军队来提升实力，虽然目前兵种差异化还谈不上特别惊艳，但组建一支由不同种族和兵种组成的混编军团，看着他们在战场上冲锋陷阵，再加上装备和道具的加成，这个游戏乐趣还是相当不错的！ 在游戏过程中，把金币存到局外用来解锁天赋树也是较为特色的机制，反正是选择存起来解锁天赋树后，让后面的开局的游戏体验爽好？还是现在当场赚钱当场花，爽了这一局再说？全由我们自己决定！选择前者的小伙伴们也不用怕，游戏的天赋树还是比较简单的，十来局的积累就能解锁完毕。其实本人心里还是希望能让天赋树变得更好的！ 整体玩下来，《桌上谈兵》最大的优点就是把肉鸽爬塔和即时战略进行了相当不错的融合。它没有《全面战争》那种复杂经营压力，却保留了排兵布阵和战场指挥的乐趣。虽然自动战斗、兵种平衡和局外成长节奏还有优化空间，但仅凭这个玩法框架，就已经足够让喜欢策略游戏的玩家投入不少时间。 [code]双语评测，认准我们： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]双语评测[/url] Make Chinese and English speaker feel at home： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]Bilingual Curator[/url][/code]

略显简陋的rogue，只能说价格符合预期。 游戏提供的选择少，收益小，简单评价就是官方似乎并不鼓励战斗，更希望通过金融的方式完成通关。 --------------------------------------------------- 为什么这么说，原因如下： 1：游戏卡牌分灰绿紫黄四阶，这本身并没什么，问题在于它每个阶都细化成了相应卡包；只要你有足够的钱，那就能在商店直接选定某阶开包，考虑到体量如此小的情况，高阶卡包基本等于必出。 2：战斗收益极小，将外部升级全解锁的情况下，游戏内一场战斗的收益从原本就固定存在的金币+X，以及招募所选族类的单位外，仅增加了一瓶药水。而战斗能提供的最大收益，却都不是这几个单一选项，而是二选一或三选一中对敌方兵种的收编。这个收编是根据对方和玩家对战的兵种间随机挑选三张，让玩家选一，因此是玩家最容易获得高阶卡的来源之一。 3：对比与收编敌方或许能获得更高阶的卡，战斗胜利我方本族卡收益通常不近如人意，一层基本就是最低价的灰色普通包，很难才会出现上位绿色罕见包。而二层和三层，却都基本是绿色罕见包，而紫色稀有包的出率甚至比一层的绿卡还要低。 4：外部升级更偏向经济，通过减少玩家产生利息所需的金币，提高出售道具的价格，增加各类槽位，降低商人卡包价格，开局选定道具等等，让玩家能以最快的方式完成财富积累，再通过商店不限量的各类卡包完成迅速的实力提升。 5：外部升级难度低：由于游戏内存在自动战斗，只需要低阶难度疯狂自动战斗，随便进入村庄存储就可，没有任何战术性，只有对于解锁的渴望。 ----------------------- 由此，我并不是很推荐，起码玩一个小时就觉得没啥游戏性，基本就是自动战斗结束。感觉也不是在爬塔，当中也没有什么运气成分，纯纯经济的比拼；而且即便运气真的那么不好，重开一局也不是多麻烦的事情，说难听些，低阶5分钟通过自动战斗就能打完一整局，能有什么娱乐性？ ----------------------- 建议：开发者对于爬塔太过于墨守成规，人家奖励提供三张，是因为本身体量不小，存在各式流派。你游因为多种族的关系，将原本体量平分了，不但让各种族显得大同小异，玩法如出一辙，那你不如多开放些选择，让更高阶的卡出现概率变相提高。 其次，别的爬塔可以信息不透明，是因为存在多种精英，对于各类流派都有好打不好打，也因此玩家才会产生要不要赌一下拼一下的心理。而你这游戏，就是由于多种族导致的扁平化，还不如公开敌人信息，让收编敌方兵种成为一种玩法。 目前虽然也能算是一种玩法，但太弱了，只能算是玩家无奈的凑数，并不能算是真正有效且存在的流派。而提前公开敌方信息，可以让玩家根据信息选定好路线，而且收编本身也是存在随机，即便没有得到玩家第一志愿，起码好歹有个安慰奖。 还有，别固定敌人种类。每层的敌人应该随机一些，也可以适当减少一些种族，将它们的方案融合到保留种族上。这样收编随机性提高了，也不存在单层敌人固定化，玩家也能选定路线。 ------------------- 就目前而言，我是给不了好评，尽管没有打到最高难度，但真的一眼望穿，没有策略性，没有娱乐性，更像是开局自动战斗——买买买——自动战斗……如此反复的游戏，没有组卡的乐趣，也没有战斗的乐趣，甚至选择路线的乐趣都没有。 说到这个，为啥爬塔的视角要设置的这么低，这么近看的很不舒服，而且甚至不能仅通过鼠标移动屏幕，还必须使用键盘wasd，设计的很不亲人。

I'm speaking as an indie dev myself. This is a great project at a very fair price. Is it as deep and polished as Creative Assembly Total War games? No. Is it as content rich as other Roguelites? No. It is, however, an extremely well thought out merger between two popular yet still relatively niche genres. It does a fantastic job blending the elements of both top down battlefield commanding as well as the randomized, progression unlocking Roguelite adventure system. Furthermore, it is getting consistent updates from a developer that actively listens to their communities feedback, including making changes for the good of the game despite not fitting with the developers own original vision. This is a damn fine developer and I wish them the best of luck in their career. For the old players, maybe check back and see if the changes they've already made have addressed some of your concerns. Progression and difficulty in particular have been explored further, and honestly on the hardest difficulties this is harder than Total War Warhammer 3 in a lot of ways. The nature of a rogue-lite makes predictable strategies harder to pull off than in Total War, and thinking on your feet and making the best of what you have is exactly what rogue genre games are best at. For new players - if you like roguelites and you like Total War, especially the Warhammer titles, don't miss this. The price is well worth the entry to have a smaller game to get your fix for conquest.
